findings.title: Part A/B re-enters loops that paused or failed on exhaustion, giving them an extra round and possibly trapping them
findings.description:
`_loop_exhaust_result` returns `PAUSED` for `on_exhaust: checkpoint` and `FAILED` for `on_exhaust: fail`, with `iteration=max_iter` (executor.py:1061-1074). Under D2, both statuses become "unfinished". Under D3, `resume_iteration_for` returns `max`, so resuming an exhausted loop runs round `max` again:
- That contradicts the design's own rule that "Resume does not grant extra rounds" (lines 180–182).
- For `on_exhaust: checkpoint`, today's behaviour is: pause for a human, then resume past the loop. After this change, resume runs one more round. If that round also fails `until:`, the loop exhausts and pauses again, so the human can't get past the loop by resuming.

The design never tells an exhaustion pause apart from an inner-checkpoint pause, and the Success Criteria (lines 298–311) have no test for either `on_exhaust` mode. The fix needs to say how resume handles each `on_exhaust` mode. For example: only re-enter when the paused round is below `max` and the pause came from an inner step, or record where the pause came from. It also needs a test for each mode.

findings.title: D1's reasoning misreads how a checkpoint resolves
findings.description:
An inner checkpoint only returns `PAUSED` when the human picks **Exit** at the interactive prompt (executor.py:1017-1025). Accept and Override continue inline, in the same round, without pausing (line 1026). That undercuts two of D1's reasons:
- **Reason 2** says resume carries out a human's choice to "Continue". A Continue choice never reaches resume at all.
- **Reason 3** says Exit stays available as the "human is taking over" option. Exit is the only path that leads to the re-entry this slice adds, so after the change, Exit followed by resume re-enters the loop. The "human takes over" reading is left with no way to express it.

Reasons 1 and 4 might still justify re-entry on their own. But D1 needs rewriting around what actually happens (Exit → PAUSED → resume), and it should say plainly that resuming after Exit now means "continue the loop".

findings.title: Resuming re-runs the paused round in full, which contradicts D1's "next round" reasoning and the round-counting rule
findings.description: Lines 164–165 say that for a loop with rounds left, "proceed" means "the next round". Lines 180–182 and the flow at line 243 (`range(start_iteration, …)` with `start_iteration` = the paused round) resume **at** the paused round. That means round N's dispatch and review, which already ran before the checkpoint, run a second time. So round N executes twice, and a loop paused at round 2 of 3 can run 4 body executions, despite "Resume does not grant extra rounds". Choose N or N+1, give the reason, and adjust the Success Criteria at lines 298–302 to match.

findings.title: Part C's WARNING leaves out the single-step loop path, which also stops silently
findings.description: D4 and the component table (line 290) put the WARNING in `_execute_loop_body` only. But `_execute_loop_step` stops on `PAUSED` silently too (executor.py:1135-1137), and D3 / line 289 already bring it into scope for `start_iteration`. Under the failure-mode rule in `.claude/rules/review-code.md`, the same abandonment on that path stays silent. Add the WARNING and its test for `_execute_loop_step`, ideally as one shared helper so the logic isn't duplicated.

findings.title: Duplicate `StepState` entries after resume are not specified
findings.description:
`_append_step` adds an entry every time a step finishes (state.py:304). After a resume, `completed_steps` holds both the old paused entry and the new one for the same `step_name`. A loop that pauses twice (round 1, resume, then round 2) leaves two paused entries.
- The design doesn't say which entry `resume_iteration_for` reads. It has to be the latest, or resume goes back to a stale round.
- It doesn't confirm that `first_unfinished_step`'s set-based check gives the right answer when entries for one name have mixed statuses.
- It doesn't say whether `load_prior_outputs` (state.py:417-436) should include the abandoned partial round's action results in `prior_outputs` for the re-entered round.

State "latest entry per step name wins" for both queries, and add a test that pauses twice.

findings.title: The flow diagram skips the CLI helpers that resume goes through
findings.description: Both resume paths call `_run_pipeline_sdk(..., from_step=...)` or `_run_pipeline(..., from_step=...)` per execution mode (run.py:1111-1131 and 1162-1180), not `execute_pipeline` directly. That's four call sites, plus the two helper signatures, that need the new iteration parameter. The component-table row "Both resume paths … pass it through" covers this, but the diagram makes the change look smaller than it is. The design should also say whether prompt-only mode can produce a paused loop at all.
